newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan listed firms Jan-March net up 43 pct-paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan listed firms Jan-March net up 43 pct-paper.

text.p: Taiwan's economy was recovering, with all 386 listed firms' net profit surging 43 percent in the first quarter to T$70.62 billion from T$49.29 billion a year earlier, the Commercial Times newspaper said on Friday.
The paper attributed the high growth to a lower base in January-March 1996, when Taiwan's economy was hurt by tensions with China.

China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a Chinese civil war split them in 1949, held a series of war games near the island to warn voters not to seek independence ahead of Taiwan's March 1996 presidential polls.
Loose liquidity spurred a stock market rally in the first quarter of 1997 and gradually boosted the property market, helping economic recovery, the paper said.
The report was based on the paper's own calculations according to results released by each firm, it said.
Financial companies enjoyed the biggest net profits, gaining T$22.51 billion, up 54.14 percent from a year ago, the paper said.
The electronics sector showed net profit of T$15.37 billion, down 16.66 percent from a year ago due to falls in prices in the semiconductor industry caused by oversupply.

Among electronics, notebook computer makers still enjoyed growth, with Compal Electronics first-quarter profit up 334 percent from a year ago and First International net up about 100 percent, it said.
Textiles earned T$5.75 billion, reversing a net loss of T$1.31 billion a year earlier, it said.
Car shares gained T$2.67 billion, also reversing a net loss of T$360 million a year ago, it said.
